title: "Flower Child"
subtitle: We must believe in the power of belief.

items.text: "Flower Child"
The sudden commotion on the shore has drawn the attention of the Manus followers.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Hey!
He pulls out a pistol, aiming it at Sophia.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: I'm warning you. Don't move!
She sighs softly.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: As expected.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: An irrational number is born irrational. It is an insurmountable divide.
Diggers stands up, positioning himself between the gun and Sophia.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Please, I'm sick of your taxonomies.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Integers, fractions, rational numbers, irrational numbers, real numbers, imaginary numbers …

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Humans are the only creatures that go to such lengths to categorize their own kind.
Sophia remains silent.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh! Not that I'm dismissing your ideas entirely. The fact that there's no conflict here already makes this place better than the world outside.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Besides, in the world beyond your island, division like that is just as common a thing.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Phrenology, physiognomy, theories of superior bloodlines …

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Every standard works to make up a class inherently entitled to more power.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: But it's all a lie! A fabricated, despicable lie!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: We should be like one family, whether on this island or in the outside world.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: The true Tower of Babel was the whole idea of class systems that people have built in our societies.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: We should stand against all of it!

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Idiot.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Is this really the time for a speech?

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Go on, grab her. We have to prevent her from using any arcane skills!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: My friend, the answer we seek is blowing in the wind.
He inserts a rose from his sleeve into the barrel of the gun.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: People of different colors, who speak different languages, raised in different cultures …

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: So much of what we are isn't chosen by us, and they should never have become barriers!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: We're all born into the same world, and we'll all die in the same world.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I wish you peace and love, my brothers and sisters.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Now, brother, don't use that waterlogged gun.
His voice is full of concern.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: It might misfire.
A geometric construct descends from the sky, binding his limbs.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Why?
Why does the road to spreading peace and love have to be so difficult?
It shouldn't be this way.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: From England to France, and from France to this island, I've said so much, but it feels like my words never turn out right.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: What do I have to do to keep conflict and strife away from this world?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: It was an impressive sermon. For a moment, my resolve wavered, and I almost believed in the world you described.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Which is precisely what frightens me.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Rhetoric often obscures the essence. That's what the School has taught me, and now I'm passing that truth on to you.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Are you saying I haven't done enough?
Sophia does not give him the answer he is hoping for.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: As for this bomb, I'll report it to the leader and let him decide accordingly.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Until a judgment is made, neither you nor your companions will be harmed.

Under the influence of an arcane skill, 

he gradually loses consciousness. 

The light before his eyes flickers and changes, and scenes flash by. 

It is as if he were drowning in a spiritual current, 

as the last rays of the sunset fade away on the silent shore.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Breaking news! Breaking news today!

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: U.S. Faces Conscription Crisis, "Medical Correction Conscription Plan" May Be Implemented!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Are today's newspaper editors feeling nostalgic?
Regent Street ?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Wait, this is Regent Street! I'm back again!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: But I'm supposed to be on the island?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Is this a side effect of their arcane skill? A dream? Memories? Or, am I dead?
Dead?
A familiar voice.
He turns to the source of it.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh, Mr. Leonard. Are you on parole now?
The voice belongs to Leonard Evans, a notorious charity scammer, who is supposed to be serving time in prison.
Diggers is another of his victims, though he doesn't realize this at the moment.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: That's quite a sense of humor, you've got.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: Just three minutes ago, you were telling me how bad you felt for not donating more. I was just about to tell you that it's not the amount that matters, but the thought.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Three minutes ago?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: He remembers.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Right! I was just about to ask. Will you personally deliver those supplies to the victims?

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: Of course, you can trust me.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Splendid.
He reaches into his pocket, then makes a troubled expression.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: If you don't have any cash, a check will do.
Diggers pulls out a handful of coins, totaling 5 pounds and 13 shillings.
Leonard sighs.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: Sir, before you engage in charity, perhaps you ought to buy yourself a meal.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Wait, Leonard, is there nothing else I can do?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I could paint posters or even some graffiti.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Or, I could create dream bubbles with my arcane skills, allowing people to glimpse a brighter future.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: Yes, certainly.
The charity scammer pauses, a smile spreading across his face.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: In fact, we're planning a charity gala.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: It's sure to be attended by some very influential people.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: I believe your dream bubbles might enhance the atmosphere, and if we can make those ladies and gentlemen happy, they'll be sure to donate even more.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: Of course, you'll be compensated. How does £50 sound?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: No, I won't do something like that. Maybe you didn't know, brother. But those upper-class rich people are the ones behind all the war and suffering in the first place!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: They make their fortunes and then use these so-called charity events as a way to avoid taxes.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: My bubbles are not for their enjoyment!
Leonard coldly chuckles.

items.speaker: Leonard
items.text: You've lost your mind, mate.
With that, he strides away.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh!
The artist wanders aimlessly along Carnaby Street.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hmm? This place … I used to love eating here, but didn't it close down?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: And these posters.
The increasing number of anomalies raises his suspicion more and more.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: The artist counts out a few coins and stops the newsboy selling papers.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: One paper, please.
He skims past numerous sensational headlines and quickly finds the date of publication.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: February 7th, 1966?
